# Copilot Instructions for PetitMonde Development

## Project Overview

PetitMonde is a full-stack application for visualizing French power networks and relationships. The project consists of three main modules:

- **Processing**: Python data pipeline (UV + Python 3.12)
- **Backend**: FastAPI REST API (UV + Python 3.12)
- **Frontend**: Vue 3 + Quasar web application (Node 24 + TypeScript)

## Frontend Tech Stack

- Vue.js 3 (Composition API with `<script setup>`)
- Quasar Framework 2.16+ (UI components + build tooling)
- TypeScript 5.9+
- Quasar CLI with Vite (build tool)
- Pinia (state management)
- Vue Router 4
- ESLint + Prettier (code quality)
- SCSS (styling)

## Backend Tech Stack

- Python 3.12
- FastAPI (REST API framework)
- Uvicorn (ASGI server)
- Pydantic v2 (data validation)
- UV (dependency management)
- Ruff (linting + formatting)

## Processing Tech Stack

- Python 3.12
- UV (dependency management)
- BeautifulSoup4 (web scraping)
- Pandas (data manipulation)
- Ruff (linting + formatting)

## Frontend Project Structure

```
frontend/src/
├── assets/         # Static assets (images, fonts)
├── boot/           # Quasar boot files (app initialization)
├── components/     # Reusable Vue components
│   ├── EssentialLink.vue
│   └── ExampleComponent.vue
├── composables/    # Composition functions (useHealthCheck, etc.)
├── config/         # App configuration (API endpoints, constants)
├── css/            # Global styles (app.scss, quasar.variables.scss)
├── layouts/        # Page layouts (MainLayout.vue)
├── pages/          # Page components (IndexPage.vue, ErrorNotFound.vue)
├── router/         # Vue Router configuration
├── services/       # API services (api.ts)
├── stores/         # Pinia stores (example-store.ts)
└── types/          # TypeScript types/interfaces
```

## Backend Project Structure

```
backend/app/
├── api/            # API routes
│   └── v1/         # API version 1
│       └── endpoints/  # Route handlers
├── core/           # Core configuration
│   ├── config.py   # Settings (Pydantic BaseSettings)
│   └── deps.py     # Dependencies
├── models/         # Data models (Pydantic)
├── services/       # Business logic
└── main.py         # FastAPI application entry point
```

## Processing Project Structure

```
processing/
├── src/            # Core modules
│   ├── api_utils.py         # LLM API interaction
│   ├── data_utils.py        # Wikipedia scraping
│   ├── relationships_utils.py  # Relationship extraction
│   └── graph_utils.py       # Graph export
├── scripts/        # Executable scripts
│   └── create_graph.py      # Main pipeline
├── tests/          # Unit tests
└── output/         # Generated data (gitignored)
```

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict TypeScript mode
- Define interfaces for all props, emits, and state
- Use type inference where possible but explicitly type complex functions
- Prefer interfaces for object definitions and type aliases for unions/intersections
- Use Generics for reusable components and functions
- Leverage Quasar's built-in types (QBtn, QInput, etc.)

## Vue Component Guidelines

- Use Single File Components (SFC) with `<script setup lang="ts">`
- Implement props validation with runtime and type checking using `defineProps<T>()`
- Keep components small and focused (max ~300 lines)
- Extract reusable logic into composables in `src/composables/`
- Use Quasar components instead of building from scratch
- Follow Quasar's component API patterns

## State Management

- Use Pinia for global state (stores in `src/stores/`)
- Prefer `ref`/`reactive` for local component state
- Structure stores by feature domain (auth, graph, filters, etc.)
- Implement proper typing for all store state, getters, and actions
- Use composables for reusable stateful logic

## Python Best Practices

### Backend (FastAPI)

- Use async/await for I/O operations
- Define Pydantic models for request/response validation
- Keep endpoints thin, business logic in services
- Use dependency injection via FastAPI's `Depends()`
- Configure CORS properly for frontend communication
- Document endpoints with docstrings (auto-generates OpenAPI docs)

### Processing

- Type hint all function parameters and returns
- Use dataclasses or Pydantic models for structured data
- Write modular, testable functions
- Handle errors gracefully with proper logging
- Cache expensive operations when appropriate

### Code Quality (Python)

- Use Ruff for both linting and formatting (replaces Black + Flake8)
- Line length: 88 characters
- Follow PEP 8 style guide
- Write docstrings for public functions/classes
- Use type hints consistently

## Testing Strategy

- **Frontend**: No test framework configured yet (TODO: add Vitest)
- **Backend**: Pytest with async support, use TestClient for API tests
- **Processing**: Pytest with coverage tracking
- Unit test composables, utilities, and business logic
- Mock external dependencies (API calls, file I/O)
- Use fixtures for reusable test data

## API Communication

- All API calls go through `src/services/api.ts` (ApiService class)
- Base URL configured in `src/config/index.ts`
- Backend runs on `http://localhost:8000` by default
- Frontend dev server on `http://localhost:9000`
- API versioned as `/api/v1/...`
- Use composables for stateful API interactions

## Performance Considerations

- Implement code-splitting with dynamic imports for routes
- Use Quasar's lazy-loading components
- Leverage Quasar's tree-shaking (only import used components)
- Use `v-memo` for expensive list rendering
- Properly memoize computed properties
- Consider Quasar's SSR mode for production if needed

## Styling Guidelines

- Use Quasar's built-in design system and utilities
- Customize via `src/css/quasar.variables.scss`
- Global styles in `src/css/app.scss`
- Use SCSS for component-scoped styles
- Leverage Quasar's spacing/color classes (q-pa-md, text-primary, etc.)
- Follow mobile-first responsive design

## Common Patterns

- Use Quasar's `useQuasar()` for programmatic components (Dialog, Notify, etc.)
- Implement error handling with try/catch in composables
- Create adapter layers for external API integration in services
- Use provide/inject sparingly (Pinia preferred for state)
- Follow SOLID principles for maintainable code

## Development Workflow

- Pre-commit hooks auto-format code (Prettier, Ruff)
- Commit messages follow conventional commits format
- Run `make lint` before pushing
- Use `make install` to set up all dependencies
- Check API docs at `http://localhost:8000/docs` when backend running

## Environment Variables

### Frontend (.env)

```env
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000
```

### Backend (.env)

```env
DEBUG=true
API_V1_PREFIX=/api/v1
BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:9000
PROCESSING_OUTPUT_PATH=../processing/output
```
